space.name: Public Organization Space
space.description: Organizations wielding delegated public authority under law: ministries, councils, delivery and research bodies, task groups, arm's-length agencies, state-owned enterprises, municipalities, and public-private hybrids.

meta.description: Five comparative representation systems for comparing public organizations, differentiated by derivation methodology, not by theme. Each system states its universe, purpose, and version, and derives its characteristic elements through one method: ontological analysis, functional analysis, relational analysis, purpose-driven analysis, or the composite-model approach. Assigning every element a value gives the comparative profile of an organization.

systems.name: ontological
systems.title: Ontological Set
systems.description: Profiles what public bodies are: their legal existence, institutional kind, composition, assets, permanence, and spatial definition. Derived by ontological analysis - enumerating the entities, kinds, and modes of existence the domain contains. Use it to compare bodies as entities before asking what they do or how they relate.
systems.provenance: authored for this atlas from the organization decomposition and agency-form comparison
systems.universe: Public organizations wielding delegated public authority under law, from ministries to municipalities. Courts included where they exercise administrative authority.
systems.purpose: Compare what bodies are: existence, kind, composition, and permanence.

elements.name: Legal Personality
elements.description: Whether the body exists as a legal subject distinct from the state or ministry.
elements.assignment_rule: Test: can it own assets and sue in its own name? If yes, separate; otherwise none.

elements.name: Institutional Position
elements.description: Where the body sits within the public institutional system.
elements.assignment_rule: Code by the body to which the organization formally answers.

elements.name: Organizational Form
elements.description: The recognized kind of public body.
elements.assignment_rule: Code by charter and function jointly; hybrids take public-private hybrid only under mixed control.

elements.name: Membership Basis
elements.description: The dominant basis on which the decision-making membership is constituted.
elements.assignment_rule: Code the basis of the majority of the deciding membership. No majority basis takes mixed.

elements.name: Asset Base
elements.description: The largest class of assets the body holds.
elements.assignment_rule: Code by balance-sheet weight. Bodies without a balance sheet take none.

elements.name: Lifecycle Stage
elements.description: The permanence of the body's constitution.
elements.assignment_rule: Read the constituting instrument: dissolution clause, renewal term, or no expiry.

elements.name: Constitutional Entrenchment
elements.description: The rank of the instrument required to abolish the body.
elements.assignment_rule: Code the highest instrument protecting it. Bodies removable by decree take executive instrument.

elements.name: Jurisdictional Scale
elements.description: The scale at which the body's authority runs.
elements.assignment_rule: Code by the polity that charters it, not by where it operates.

elements.name: Budgetary Identity
elements.description: The body's financial existence as a budgetary unit.
elements.assignment_rule: Code by the last full-year accounts. Bodies spending only through a parent vote take subsumed vote.

elements.name: Territorial Definition
elements.description: Whether and how the body's remit is spatially bounded.
elements.assignment_rule: Code bounded where a defined territory delimits the remit; functional where remit follows a task; network where several territories are covered jointly.

elements.name: Mandate Scope
elements.description: How wide the chartered remit runs.
elements.assignment_rule: Count the domains named in the charter, not those grown by practice.

systems.name: functional
systems.title: Functional Set
systems.description: Profiles what public bodies do: the task families they perform, coded by exercised activity rather than charter rhetoric. Derived by functional analysis - enumerating the functions and activities of the domain. Use it to compare workloads and task portfolios across bodies with different legal forms.
systems.provenance: authored for this atlas from the function taxonomy and agency mandates
systems.universe: Public organizations wielding delegated public authority under law, from ministries to municipalities. Courts included where they exercise administrative authority.
systems.purpose: Compare what bodies do: task families by exercised activity.

elements.name: Policy Formulation
elements.description: Whether the body formulates policy.
elements.assignment_rule: Code lead where its drafts normally become policy; contributor where consulted; none otherwise.

elements.name: Service Delivery
elements.description: Whether the body delivers services to end users.
elements.assignment_rule: Code direct where its own staff meet users; commissioned where it funds others to deliver.

elements.name: Regulation
elements.description: Whether the body makes binding rules for others.
elements.assignment_rule: Code the highest exercised in the last three years.

elements.name: Enforcement
elements.description: Whether the body compels compliance.
elements.assignment_rule: Code the highest exercised in the last three years. Inspection without sanction stays inspection.

elements.name: Adjudication
elements.description: Whether the body decides individual cases with binding effect.
elements.assignment_rule: Code binding only where decisions are enforceable without further approval.

elements.name: Revenue Handling
elements.description: Whether the body handles public money beyond spending its budget.
elements.assignment_rule: Code collection where it levies; fund management where it stewards earmarked funds.

elements.name: Research and Evidence
elements.description: Whether the body produces evidence for policy.
elements.assignment_rule: Code in-house where dedicated research staff exist on establishment.

elements.name: Coordination
elements.description: Whether the body coordinates other bodies.
elements.assignment_rule: Code lead where it convenes and sets the agenda of a standing coordination arrangement.

elements.name: Oversight of Others
elements.description: Whether the body supervises other public bodies.
elements.assignment_rule: Code supervisory only with a formal oversight mandate over named bodies.

elements.name: Commercial Operation
elements.description: Whether the body operates commercially.
elements.assignment_rule: Code by the pricing rule of its trading activity. Leave unset where no trading exists.

elements.name: Emergency Powers
elements.description: Whether the body holds extraordinary powers.
elements.assignment_rule: Code standing where powers are exercisable without fresh authorization.

systems.name: relational
systems.title: Relational Set
systems.description: Profiles how public bodies stand toward others: principals, overseers, peers, clients, contractors, and publics. Derived by relational analysis - enumerating the relationships between bodies and their constituent elements. Use it to compare positions in the institutional web rather than intrinsic traits.
systems.provenance: authored for this atlas from the coordination and accountability analysis
systems.universe: Public organizations wielding delegated public authority under law, from ministries to municipalities. Courts included where they exercise administrative authority.
systems.purpose: Compare how bodies stand: principals, peers, clients, and overseers.

elements.name: Political Principal
elements.description: The political body the organization answers to.
elements.assignment_rule: Code the body that appoints, directs, or dismisses the leadership.

elements.name: Oversight Forum
elements.description: The forum before which the body must answer.
elements.assignment_rule: Code the forum that can compel attendance and answers. Two or more active forums take multiple.

elements.name: Hierarchical Subordination
elements.description: The body's place in a chain of command.
elements.assignment_rule: Code subordinate where orders flow downward as of right; arm's-length where direction needs instruments; independent where no direction lies.

elements.name: Peer Coordination
elements.description: The body's role among peer bodies.
elements.assignment_rule: Code lead where it convenes peers; isolated where no standing peer arrangement exists.

elements.name: Client Relation
elements.description: Whom the body directly serves.
elements.assignment_rule: Code by the primary end user of its dominant activity. Pure staff functions take none.

elements.name: Contract Relations
elements.description: The weight of contracting in the body's operations.
elements.assignment_rule: Code major where contracted spend exceeds one quarter of the budget.

elements.name: Intergovernmental Ties
elements.description: Relations with other levels of government.
elements.assignment_rule: Code federal relations only in federal polities; unitary command where lower levels obey; none where single-level.

elements.name: International Ties
elements.description: Relations beyond the state.
elements.assignment_rule: Code treaty-mandated only with a binding international obligation to cooperate.

elements.name: Shared-Service Ties
elements.description: The body's position in shared-service arrangements.
elements.assignment_rule: Code by the dominant direction of shared-service flows in the last full year.

elements.name: Public Answerability
elements.description: Whether the body answers directly to the public.
elements.assignment_rule: Code direct with elected leadership or mandatory public hearings; mediated with published reporting; none otherwise.

systems.name: purpose-driven
systems.title: Purpose-Driven Set
systems.description: Profiles what decision-makers need to know: autonomy, answerability, reformability, comparability, and risk. Derived by purpose-driven analysis - starting from the questions, decisions, and analytical tasks the comparison must support, then selecting the elements that answer them. Use it when a decision, not a description, is the output.
systems.frame_basis: Purpose-driven analysis from canonical comparison questions
systems.provenance: authored for this atlas from the evaluation and governance questions
systems.universe: Public organizations wielding delegated public authority under law, from ministries to municipalities. Courts included where they exercise administrative authority.
systems.purpose: Answer decisions: autonomy, answerability, reformability, comparability, risk.

elements.name: Autonomy Grade
elements.description: The overall freedom of the body from day-to-day political direction.
elements.assignment_rule: Code high with case independence plus own revenue or statute; low under direct command; medium otherwise.

elements.name: Accountability Depth
elements.description: Whether answerability carries consequences.
elements.assignment_rule: Code full where a completed accountability cycle has removed or sanctioned leadership in the body's history or class.

elements.name: Reformability
elements.description: How the body can be reorganized or abolished.
elements.assignment_rule: Code by the instrument needed for abolition, as with entrenchment.

elements.name: Comparability Class
elements.description: The peer group against which the body should be compared.
elements.assignment_rule: Assign by form and function family jointly; genuinely unique constitutional bodies take sui generis.

elements.name: Risk Bearer
elements.description: Who bears the financial residual risk.
elements.assignment_rule: Code by who absorbs a deficit in practice, not in theory.

elements.name: Performance Visibility
elements.description: How observable the body's performance is to outsiders.
elements.assignment_rule: Code published with regularly released indicators; internal where measurement stays inside.

elements.name: Mandate Clarity
elements.description: How precisely the mandate states what success looks like.
elements.assignment_rule: Code from the current mandate documents, not from practice.

elements.name: Capture Exposure
elements.description: Exposure to capture by concentrated interests.
elements.assignment_rule: Code low with tenure protections plus transparency duties; high with revolving-door leadership and concentrated regulated interests; medium otherwise.

elements.name: Continuity Guarantee
elements.description: Assurance that the body persists.
elements.assignment_rule: Read the constituting instrument for expiry and renewal terms.

elements.name: Sunset Provision
elements.description: Whether termination is programmed.
elements.assignment_rule: Code sunset with a date in statute; review clause with a mandated periodic review.

systems.name: model-derived
systems.title: Model-Derived Set
systems.description: Derives characteristic elements from an overarching model of the public organization: chartered authority made operable through mandate, principals, governance, agency, execution, resources, accountability, and ecology. Each submodel contributes its elements; together they form one comparative profile. The composite-model approach worked as a system.
systems.frame_basis: Composite-model approach: overarching Public Organization Model in eight submodels
systems.provenance: authored as a new model decomposition for this atlas
systems.universe: Public organizations wielding delegated public authority under law, from ministries to municipalities. Courts included where they exercise administrative authority.
systems.purpose: Full-model profiling: every submodel contributes elements to one profile.

elements.name: Legal Constitution
elements.description: Charter submodel: the legal basis of existence.
elements.assignment_rule: Cite the constituting instrument.

elements.name: Mandate Scope
elements.description: Charter submodel: how wide the chartered remit runs.
elements.assignment_rule: Count the domains named in the charter, not those grown by practice.

elements.name: Political Principal
elements.description: Principal submodel: the political body answered to.
elements.assignment_rule: Code the body that appoints, directs, or dismisses the leadership.

elements.name: Direction Instruments
elements.description: Principal submodel: the instruments carrying current objectives.
elements.assignment_rule: Code the instrument whose breach has consequences.

elements.name: Governing Structure
elements.description: Governance submodel: the arrangement deciding direction.
elements.assignment_rule: Code the body that can overrule the chief executive.

elements.name: Leadership Form
elements.description: Agency submodel: how executive responsibility is held.
elements.assignment_rule: Code the title holding residual executive authority.

elements.name: Decision Rights
elements.description: Agency submodel: who may decide what, within which limits.
elements.assignment_rule: Test with a contested decision: whose signature settles it.

elements.name: Functions
elements.description: Execution submodel: the task family performed.
elements.assignment_rule: Code by mandate-weighted dominant family, using budget shares where published.

elements.name: Operational Deployment
elements.description: Execution submodel: geographic distribution of mandated activities.
elements.assignment_rule: Map where activities are performed, not where staff sit.

elements.name: Funding Regime
elements.description: Resource submodel: the revenue base.
elements.assignment_rule: Code by the largest revenue share over the last full year.

elements.name: Personnel Regime
elements.description: Resource submodel: how people are employed and managed.
elements.assignment_rule: Code career-based where entry is by examination into a corps with tenure; position-based where posts are filled openly on contract.

elements.name: Accountability Line
elements.description: Accountability submodel: the monitoring arrangement with consequences.
elements.assignment_rule: Code the arrangement that can trigger leadership consequences.

elements.name: Institutional Position
elements.description: Ecology submodel: the place in the public system.
elements.assignment_rule: Code by the body to which the organization formally answers.
